posts.title: Your RAG system is probably broken
tweets:
Your RAG system is probably broken.

And you don't know it because you're not measuring the right things.

Here's what I learned building YouTubeRAG (thread):

1/ The Common Mistakes

• Fixed-size chunks (breaks mid-thought)
• Pure vector search (misses exact matches)
• No source attribution (can't verify)
• Giant context windows (slow, expensive)

Most RAG tutorials teach these.

2/ Chunking Strategy Matters

Don't split on character count.

Use semantic boundaries:
• Topic changes
• Speaker transitions
• Natural pauses

SpaCy can detect these automatically.

3/ Hybrid Search Wins

Vector search: "What's the concept?"
Keyword search: "Where's the exact term?"

Use both.

My YouTubeRAG combines semantic + keyword.
Retrieval quality: dramatically better.

4/ Metadata is Crucial

Store with each chunk:
• Source document
• Timestamp/position
• Original context
• Confidence score

You'll need these for verification and navigation.

5/ Context Window Management

Don't stuff everything in.

Retrieve relevant chunks → rerank → take top K.

Less context = faster, cheaper, often more accurate.

6/ Test Your Retrieval

Before connecting to an LLM:
• Query the vector DB directly
• Check if right chunks return
• Measure precision/recall

Bad retrieval + good LLM = garbage output.

7/ The Meta-Lesson

RAG isn't about the model.

It's about:
• How you chunk
• How you embed
• How you retrieve

Fix the pipeline. Then worry about the model.

posts.title: How I debug automation failures systematically
tweets:
How I debug automation failures systematically.

My scheduler broke for 3 days. Here's how I fixed it (thread):

1/ The Symptom

60 agents weren't running.
No errors in logs.
Scheduler started fine.

Silent failure. The worst kind.

2/ Step 1: Verify the Basics

• Is the script executable?
• Are paths correct?
• Are dependencies installed?
• Are env vars set?

Often the fix is embarrassingly simple.

3/ Step 2: Trace the Execution

Add logging at every step:
• Script started
• Each agent triggered
• Each agent completed
• Errors caught

Find where execution stops.

4/ Step 3: Check Environment

Cron/LaunchAgent run in different env than terminal.

• Different PATH
• Different working directory
• Different permissions

Print env vars. Compare to manual run.

5/ The Root Cause

Hardcoded path: /Users/old/path/to/project

Worked until I moved folders.

Scheduler tried to access non-existent path.
Failed silently because of error handling.

Lesson: Never hardcode paths.

6/ The Fix

• Use relative paths
• Use environment variables
• Make error handling loud, not quiet
• Add health checks that alert on failure

7/ The Prevention

Now every agent has:
• Verbose logging option
• Health check endpoint
• Failure alerts
• Self-healing restart logic

Silent failures are now impossible.

2. Fail loud, not quiet
That error handler that silently catches exceptions? It's hiding disasters. Make failures visible.

3. Health checks matter
Now every agent reports "I ran" to a central log. No report = something's wrong.

4. Redundancy in monitoring
Single point of failure in monitoring = you don't know when things fail.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁

Your RAG system is probably broken.

And you don't know it because you're not measuring the right things.

• Fixed-size chunks (breaks mid-thought)
• Pure vector search (misses exact matches)
• No source attribution (can't verify)
• Giant context windows (slow, expensive)

Most RAG tutorials teach these exact patterns.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

1. Chunking strategy
Don't split on character count. Use semantic boundaries.
Topic changes. Speaker transitions. Natural pauses.
SpaCy can detect these automatically.

2. Hybrid search
Vector search: "What's the concept?"
Keyword search: "Where's the exact term?"
Use both. My YouTubeRAG combines semantic + keyword.

3. Metadata preservation
Store source, timestamp, context with each chunk.
You'll need these for verification and navigation.

4. Test your retrieval
Before connecting to an LLM:
• Query the vector DB directly
• Check if right chunks return
• Measure precision/recall

Bad retrieval + good LLM = garbage output.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗮-𝗟𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗼𝗻

RAG isn't about the model.
It's about the pipeline.

Fix chunking. Add hybrid search. Test retrieval.
Then worry about which LLM to use.
